title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-17

ai_review.summary: Muddy audience tape but features an outstanding acoustic set highlighted by Box of Rain and a soaring Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The recording is an old‑generation audience capture that suffers from muffled mids, a persistent high‑pitched whine and limited instrument separation, especially in the electric portion.  Despite the sonic flaws, listeners rave about the historic acoustic set – the only known full‑band rendition of "Box of Rain" – and praise the Dark Star, Friend of the Devil and Ripple as show‑highlights.

ai_rating.rationale: The performance is repeatedly praised (acoustic set, Box of Rain, Dark Star) while the audio quality is consistently described as poor; weighting show quality higher yields a rating above average but not stellar.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muddy mids, barely audible pedal steel and piano on Box of Rain, persistent high‑pitched whine throughout, electric set clouded and difficult to discern; overall listenable but far from clean.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A superb, fully‑realized acoustic first set (with NRPS guests) is the highlight; the electric second set is energetically performed but hampered by the recording's cloudiness.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s piano on Box of Rain is faintly audible and praised for adding depth to the acoustic set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s vocal lead on Box of Rain is noted as strong; his bass work isn’t specifically discussed due to recording limits.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pedal steel and piano (Pigpen) can be almost made out on Box of Rain, though the overall keyboard presence is muffled.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums receive praise for energy during Dark Star and the jam sections, despite being clouded in the mix.
